Perform WF-02 Step 2d (idiom review, HARD GATE) for REQ-373 per docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md, using your existing procedure in .claude/agents/reviewer.md: idiomatic OTP vs. crutch, supervision integrity, type-safety gaps, scope creep, consistency with docs/migration/decisions/ records. Read `git diff origin/main...HEAD` yourself.

Specifically confirm: (1) SCOPE -- PLC-01/module_ref catalog versioning was NOT touched or built (grep the diff for any module_ref resolution logic that shouldn't be there); (2) SCOPE -- no file under web/ was modified anywhere in this diff; (3) lib/letflow/engine/pin_resolver.ex's existing PIN-01..05 machinery was NOT modified beyond the Engine.create/2 pin_lookup/2 call-site change (this is released, tested machinery per the requirement text -- confirm ELIXIR-DEV didn't refactor it); (4) idiom -- publish/3 and retire/1 in service_catalog.ex use proper Ecto transactions/changesets, not ad-hoc Repo calls; (5) SECURITY-REVIEWER flagged one design open question (OQ-1: no FK from service_catalog_versions back to service_catalog, to avoid changing delete/1's error contract) -- confirm or override this tradeoff explicitly in your verdict; (6) decision-record consistency -- confirm the schema decision (in-place status column + sibling archive table) doesn't contradict any docs/migration/decisions/ record; (7) moduledoc quality -- confirm the schema-decision reasoning (AC1), retire-vs-fallback decision (AC4), and PLC-01 out-of-scope citation (AC7) are all actually present and substantively stated in the new/changed moduledocs, not just claimed in the handoff. FAIL if a genuine crutch, broken supervision, or scope creep is found; otherwise PASS with any non-blocking notes recorded. Set this handoff's status to COMPLETED with your genuine independent verdict, commit and push before ending your turn.

findings.1_plc01_scope: CONFIRMED clean. grep for module_ref across the full diff shows only moduledoc prose citing it as explicitly OUT of scope (entry.ex, service_catalog.ex, pin_lookup.ex all state this). Letflow.ServiceCatalog.PinLookup.build/0's module_lookup field is copied verbatim from PinResolver.default_lookup/0 (permanent {:error, :not_found} stub) -- no module_ref resolution logic of any kind was built.
findings.2_web_untouched: CONFIRMED. `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat` shows zero files under web/ -- all 22 changed files are lib/, priv/repo/migrations/, test/, docs/, and handoffs/.
findings.3_pin_resolver_untouched: CONFIRMED. `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/engine/pin_resolver.ex` is empty -- the file was not touched at all. The only Engine-side change is engine.ex's pin_lookup/2 private helper, which swaps PinResolver.default_lookup() for PinLookup.build() on one line, with attrs[:pin_lookup] passthrough and the prefix-unused contract both preserved unchanged. This matches the requirement's own constraint that PIN-01..05 is released, tested machinery not to be refactored.
findings.4_idiom_ecto: Idiomatic. publish/3 runs inside Repo.transaction/1 via a private do_publish/3 using a `with`/else->Repo.rollback chain (fetch current row, check_publishable_version, archive_current_version via Version.archive_changeset/1 + Repo.insert, apply_publish via Entry.publish_changeset/2 + Repo.update). retire/1 uses Entry.retire_changeset/1 + Repo.update, explicit :already_retired instead of a silent idempotent :ok (matches the codebase's stated 'no silent no-op' discipline). No raw Repo.query/SQL string-building in either function -- SECURITY-REVIEWER's own grep for Repo.query across the diff already confirmed zero hits. No crutch found (no ad-hoc Repo.update_all bypassing a changeset, no hand-rolled state machine standing in for gen_statem/changeset validation -- this is plain CRUD-shaped domain logic, not a state-machine-shaped problem, so GenServer/gen_statem concerns don't apply here to begin with).
findings.5_oq1_fk_tradeoff: REVIEWER DECISION: CONFIRM the no-FK tradeoff as shipped (no rework needed). service_catalog_versions is an append-only audit/archive table with no live-resolution role (PinLookup.catalog_lookup/1 only ever reads the current service_catalog row, never the archive table) -- an orphaned archive row after a rare admin delete/1 is a referential-integrity blemish, not a correctness or security hazard, and the alternative (ON DELETE CASCADE) would silently expand delete/1's error/behavior contract beyond what this requirement's ACs asked for, which is the right thing to avoid mid-requirement. This is exactly the kind of scope-fence discipline REQ-373's SCOPE FENCE calls for. Worth a follow-up issue only if RELEASE-VALIDATOR or a future requirement decides archive-row hygiene on delete matters -- not blocking here.
findings.6_decision_record_consistency: CONFIRMED no contradiction. Searched docs/migration/decisions/ for every file mentioning 'version' (0001, 0003, 0004, 0005, 0009, 0010, 0012, 0014, 0016, 0018, 0019, 0020, 0021, 0022, 0023, 0024, 0026, 0027, 0029, 0030, 0033, 0036). None mandate a composite-key versioned-entity shape or forbid a status-column-plus-sibling-archive-table shape; 0003 (ecto-schema-strategy)'s own versioning example is a tenant-scoped unique constraint pattern (uq_definition_tenant_version), not a composite-PK requirement, and is about a different, tenant-scoped table -- service_catalog's global-table status (itself a REVIEWER-signed-off pre-existing divergence, per SECURITY-REVIEWER's INV-1 finding) is inherited, not re-litigated, by this migration. No conflict.
findings.7_moduledoc_quality: CONFIRMED substantively present, not just claimed. lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex's moduledoc has a full dedicated '## REQ-373 -- version/status lifecycle: THE SCHEMA DECISION' section with 4 numbered reasoning points (AC1) plus a separate PLC-01-out-of-scope section (AC7) citing pin_resolver.ex's SCOPE GAP language by name. entry.ex's moduledoc restates the schema decision, states the Ecto.Enum casing convention rationale, and has its own retire-vs-fallback paragraph (AC4) plus its own PLC-01-out-of-scope paragraph (AC7). retire/1's own @doc has the most detailed AC4 reasoning (structural 'at most one live row' argument, explicit rejection of silent reactivation, and a distinct explanation of why pin_for/3 is structurally unaffected). None of these are placeholder or one-line claims -- all three ACs are substantively reasoned in prose, in multiple locations, cross-referencing each other correctly.
